newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputy says re-election bill will pass -TV.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputy says re-election bill will pass -TV.

text.p: The government leader in Brazil's lower house said he expects a bill allowing re-election of sitting presidents to be approved with more than 340 votes, a local television reported on Monday.
"We are confident of the victory. We will approve the amendment with more than 340 votes," deputy Benito Gama, from the Liberal Front Party (PFL), told TV Globo.

The re-election amendment, which would give President Fernando Henrique Cardoso the chance of running for a second term, is expected to be put to a first full vote in the Chamber of Deputies Tuesday or Wednesday.
The amendment needs 308 votes to be approved.
Gama also said he expected deputies to approve the amendment when it goes for a second vote in the lower house.
"There is no reason for changing the vote in the second round," Gama told the television.
